chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Abu Basir and Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding
the boy who is ten years old making a will, he said: 'When he reaches the place of the will, it is valid.'
ai.seo_question: At what age is a boy considered capable of making a valid will in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a ten-year-old boy possesses limited testamentary capacity (*ahliyyat al-wasiyyah*), allowing him to dispose of his property through a will. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling distinguishes between full legal maturity and the specific capacity to make a *wasiyyah*, which is valid provided the child understands the nature of the disposition, reflecting the principle that wisdom (*hikmah*) can manifest at a young age.
